commits.comment: 新增 SfaRemoteD2HConnector，将 SFA KV cache 从远端 Prefill NPU 通过 MemFabric pull 模式直接传输到 Decode 侧 CPU pinned pool（main K/V）和 rank-local HBM（indexer KV）。这是一个完整的 KV Connector V1 实现，包含协议层（protocol.py）、D 侧读线程（read_thread.py）、P 侧发送线程（send_thread.py）、两侧调度器（scheduler.py）和 worker（worker.py），以及进程级 MemFabric 单例引擎（memfabric_transfer_engine.py）。该连接器支持不等价 TP（p_tp >= d_tp 且整除，contributor group 机制）、OpenAI prompt 列表批量展开、层级就绪/完成传播、传输重试与优雅关闭。同时修改了 AscendMultiConnector 以支持 layerwise PD completion 顺序控制（PD provider 先于 store），并重构了 layerwise_cache_layout：从按完整 cache signature 分组改为按 main cache spec 分组，indexer cache 作为子集跟随 main 共享；修复了 MTP 场景下 layerwise load 使用安全范围的问题（use_eagle），并让 SFA attention 在每层 scatter 完成后调用 notify_kv_cache_written。该 PR 风险较高，涉及多模块协同、新协议和新线程模型，且改变了 layerwise buffer 复用的既有语义。

commits.message:
[Feature][KV Transfer] Add SFA PD RD2H connector for kv cache offload (#12831)

## What this PR does / why we need it

Building on the sparse decode offload support introduced in #13026, this
PR introduces `SFAPDRD2HConnector`, a decode-offload-specific connector
for transferring SFA KV cache from remote Prefill workers directly into
Decode-side storage.

The connector uses a MemFabric pull-based RD2H path:

- Main SFA K/V is transferred into the Decode-side pinned CPU KV cache
pool managed by `KVOffloadDecodeManager`.
- Indexer KV is transferred into rank-local device memory.
- Prefill workers expose their KV addresses and notify Decode workers
when each layer is ready.
- Decode workers own the transfer destinations and pull the required KV
data before the request enters decode execution.

The implementation also provides:

- Separate main/indexer cache mappings.
- Multi-TP rank mapping and transfer ownership.
- Batched request handling.
- Layer-level readiness and completion propagation.
- Transfer retry, error reporting, and graceful shutdown.
- Integration with `AscendMultiConnector`.
- A diagnostic tool for validating MemFabric RD2H transfers.

The connector implementation is located under `kv_p2p/sfa_pd_rd2h`
because it transfers KV data between disaggregated Prefill and Decode
instances.

This is a stacked PR based on the Decode offload PR. Layerwise Prefill
KV pool reuse and sparse-C8 compatibility are outside the scope of this
PR and will be submitted separately.

Related RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48203

## Performance

This PR introduces KV cache offloading to enable serving sequences of up
to 1M tokens. On GLM-5.2:

- During Prefill, it reduces the peak HBM footprint of the KV cache by
up to 90%, with no significant degradation in end-to-end performance.
- During Decode, it reduces the peak HBM footprint of the KV cache by
more than 90% and supports up to nine concurrent 1M-token sequences.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. It introduces a new KV connector named `SFAPDRD2HConnector`.

Configuration and deployment documentation will be provided in a
follow-up documentation PR.

commits.message:
[BugFix] Support virtual requests in Mooncake connector (#13669)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds support for the optional `do_virtual` flag in
`MooncakeConnector`.

When `do_virtual` is enabled for a decode-side KV receive request, this
change:

- propagates `do_virtual` from `kv_transfer_params` to `ReqMeta`;
- marks the request as completed through
  `KVCacheTaskTracker.add_not_transfer_request`;
- skips submitting the request to the remaining Mooncake KV receive and
  transfer path.

This is needed for virtual execution flows where the decode-side request
should follow the normal KV transfer completion path without performing
an actual remote KV cache receive operation.

The default value of `do_virtual` is `False`, so the existing Mooncake
KV transfer behavior remains unchanged when the flag is not specified.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

This PR adds an optional `do_virtual` field to the per-request
`kv_transfer_params` handled by `MooncakeConnector`.

When `do_virtual` is set to `True`, the decode-side KV receive request
is
marked as completed through `add_not_transfer_request`, and the actual
Mooncake KV receive path is skipped.

When the field is omitted or set to `False`, the existing behavior is
unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- Ran Ruff lint checks:

```bash
ruff check \
  vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py
```

- Formatted the modified file with Ruff:

```bash
ruff format \
  vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py
```

- Ran a Python syntax check:

```bash
python -m py_compile \
  vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py
```

- Manually tested the change in an Ascend 1P1D deployment with:
  - `MooncakeConnectorV1`
  - Prefill TP size: 2
  - Decode TP size: 2
  - Model: `Qwen3-30B-A3B-W8A8`

- Sent a decode-side request with `do_virtual=true` and dummy remote KV
  transfer metadata.

- Temporarily added a log in the `do_virtual` branch and verified that:
  - the request entered the virtual completion branch;
  - `add_not_transfer_request` was executed;
  - the subsequent Mooncake KV transfer scheduling path was skipped;
  - the decode server completed the request and returned a response
    successfully without performing an actual remote KV cache transfer.

The temporary validation log was removed from the final patch.

No automated test was added. The change was validated through the manual
Ascend 1P1D smoke test described above.

commits.message:
[CI][E2E] Make multi-node config paths explicit for nightly and weekly tests (#13978)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR makes the config path explicit for A2/A3 multi-node nightly and
weekly tests.

Previously:

- Nightly multi-node jobs did not pass `config_base_path`, so external
DP cases could incorrectly fall back to the internal DP test runner.
- Weekly A3 selected internal or external DP through hardcoded job-level
paths, making its behavior inconsistent with nightly tests.

This PR:

- Passes `matrix.test_config.config_base_path` through the Nightly A2,
Nightly A3, and Weekly A3 multi-node workflows.
- Adds an explicit `config_base_path` to every current A2/A3 multi-node
test case.
- Supports internal and external DP cases consistently in both the
`multi_node` and `double_node` matrices.
- Removes the implicit config-path fallback so newly added multi-node
cases must declare their config directory.
- Removes weekly matrix entries whose referenced YAML files are not
present in the weekly config directory.

This prevents external DP cases from being routed through the internal
DP test entry and makes the test configuration easier to understand and
maintain.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is a CI/E2E test configuration change only.

### How was this patch tested?

By running the test.

commits.message: [Misc] Upgrade CANN(9.1.0), PTA(2.10.0.post4), and Triton(3.2.2) (#13901) ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR upgrades the dependency stack used by the `main` branch: - Upgrade CANN from 9.0.1 to 9.1.0. - Replace the 310P 9.1.0 beta images with the 9.1.0 final images. - Synchronize A2, A3, A5, and 310P images across Ubuntu, openEuler, existing wheel builds, CI, nightly tests, and CSRC cache jobs. - Upgrade PTA (`torch-npu`) from 2.10.0.post2 to 2.10.0.post4. - Upgrade Triton Ascend from 3.2.1 to 3.2.2. - Update dependency metadata, installation documentation, Dockerfiles, CI image tags, and CANN package requirements accordingly. - Keep UVA disabled for Triton Ascend 3.2.2 because it is still affected by the pinned-memory pointer validation issue tracked in [triton-ascend#783](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton-ascend/issues/783). The platform configuration propagation change is cherry-picked from [#13799](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/13799), originally authored by @yiz-liu. This change synchronizes platform-derived Ascend configuration overrides back to `vllm_config.additional_config`. This ensures that spawned EngineCore and worker processes reconstruct the effective values of `enable_npugraph_ex`, `enable_static_kernel`, and `recompute_scheduler_enable` instead of restoring stale defaults. #### GDN unit test compatibility After upgrading CANN and torch-npu, `torch_npu.npu_chunk_gated_delta_rule` becomes available and the GDN fused-op probe succeeds. This causes `test_npu_connector_observes_updated_gdn_state_after_compile` to enter the real fused CANN path instead of the mocked Triton path. The test was originally added to verify that the layerwise KV connector observes updated convolution and SSM states after eager and `torch.compile` executions. Its numerical kernels are intentionally mocked, and it uses lightweight FP32 tensors with a head dimension of 2. These inputs do not satisfy the fused CANN operator constraints, which require BF16 query inputs and production-compatible dimensions. Explicitly mock `_probe_fused_chunk()` to return `False` in this test so it continues using the mocked Triton path. This keeps the test focused on the KV connector and compilation behavior without changing production GDN behavior. - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/31356537202/job/93361160358?pr=13901#step:17:3286 ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? ### How was this patch tested? - vLLM version: v0.26.0 - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/0351e9aa1fdf1a51329d1906881528dfe61fc88e --------- Signed-off-by: MrZ20 <2609716663@qq.com>

commits.message:
[CI] Improve workflow cancellation behavior (#13949)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
GitHub Actions reevaluates job and step conditions when a workflow is
cancelled. Conditions using `always()` remain true during cancellation,
which may keep dependent jobs queued or running, especially when custom
runners or reusable workflows are involved. This can prevent
`concurrency.cancel-in-progress` and normal UI cancellation from
promptly terminating an old run.

This PR improves cancellation behavior for non-nightly workflows:

- Replaces necessary failure-handling conditions with `!cancelled()`,
allowing jobs such as artifact uploads and failure reports to run after
failures while skipping them after cancellation.
- Removes redundant `always()` conditions where jobs should only run
after their dependencies succeed.
- Updates PR tests, E2E reporting, pre-commit cache handling, Main2Main,
estimated-time updates, and weekly workflows.
- Leaves nightly workflows unchanged because some nightly jobs require
unconditional cleanup or coordination.

commits.message:
[Feature][MRV2] SFA model runner v2 adaptation (#13069)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds the missing Sparse Flash Attention (SFA) indexer support to
the Ascend Model Runner V2.

SFA models such as GLM-5 and DeepSeek-V3.2 use an additional indexer
cache besides the normal attention KV cache. The Ascend Model Runner V1
already supports this cache layout, but the corresponding Model Runner
V2 path did not
properly describe, allocate, reshape, bind, or prepare metadata for the
indexer cache.

As a result, SFA models could fail during either engine initialization
or request execution when Model Runner V2 was enabled.

This PR completes the non-C8 SFA indexer path by:

- Recognizing `DeepseekV32IndexerCache` during Model Runner V2 KV-cache
specification.
- Reusing the existing `AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec` and
`AscendSFAIndexerBackend` implementations.
- Allocating and reshaping the indexer cache as an independent
single-tensor cache.
- Reusing the existing Ascend `bind_kv_cache` implementation to bind
multiple cache modules belonging to the same model layer, including the
normal attention cache and `indexer.k_cache`.
- Passing the padded input-token count to the Ascend attention metadata
builder so that positions, slot mapping, and RoPE metadata are
consistent with the actual Model Runner V2 input.
- Keeping the existing SFA cache composition flow, which combines the
normal KV cache and indexer cache before invoking the Ascend SFA
kernels.

The implementation intentionally reuses the existing Model Runner V1 and
Ascend SFA components where possible. It does not introduce a new
cache-spec class, attention backend, cache-binding implementation, or
patch file.

Scope：This PR currently supports the non-C8 SFA indexer-cache path.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

There are no changes to the public API, CLI arguments, model
configuration, or launch scripts.

commits.message:
[BugFix][SFA] Guard DSA-CP graph padding sequence lengths (#13779)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This extends the DSA-CP graph-padding safeguard from
[2b1ac612496e8306c6d7d95d175e93fad90057b1](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/2b1ac612496e8306c6d7d95d175e93fad90057b1)
to the equivalent metadata construction path in `sfa_v1.py`.

The SFA v1 metadata builder could calculate `seq_lens - offset` for a
graph-padding request whose global `seq_lens` is zero. When a padded
four-token slot crosses a rank-local boundary, this can produce a
negative `actual_seq_lengths_key` and pass invalid metadata to sparse
attention.

This PR:

- requires both a non-empty local request slice and a positive global
sequence length;
- clamps candidate rank-local key sequence lengths to zero;
- adds a regression test for the TP=8, graph-size=80, MTP3-style rank-6
boundary case.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or configuration changes.

It prevents invalid negative SFA key sequence metadata for affected
DSA-CP graph-padding layouts.

### How was this patch tested?

Added `test_dsa_cp_metadata_builder_masks_graph_padding` in
`tests/ut/attention/a2/test_sfa_v1.py`. The test reproduces the TP=8,
graph-size=80, rank-6 boundary case and verifies padded local key
sequence lengths are zero and all generated lengths are non-negative.

Local checks completed:

- `git diff --check`
- Ruff lint and format checks for both changed Python files
- codespell for both changed Python files
- Python AST syntax parsing for both changed Python files

The `torch/torch_npu` unit test was not executed on the local PC because
this repository requires NPU-dependent tests to run in an Ascend
container. Run:

```bash
pytest -sv tests/ut/attention/a2/test_sfa_v1.py::TestAscendSFAMetadataBuilder::test_dsa_cp_metadata_builder_masks_graph_padding
```
